questions.question: Which security mechanism controls record-level access to data in ServiceNow?

options.text: Roles
Groups
Access Control Lists (ACLs)
Data Policies

explanation.correct: Access Control Lists (ACLs) control record-level and field-level access to data. ACLs specify what tables, fields, and operations users can access based on roles and conditions. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Roles grant access to application modules and menus, but ACLs control the actual data access.
Groups organize users and can be assigned roles, but they don't directly control data access.
Data Policies enforce data integrity rules on forms, not access control.

source.excerpt: Most security settings are implemented using access controls. In addition to restricting CRUD operations, access control rules can restrict ServiceNow specific operations on tables and fields.

questions.question: What role is required to modify Access Control Lists (ACLs) in ServiceNow?

options.text: admin
security_admin
acl_admin
itil

explanation.correct: The security_admin role is required to modify Access Control Lists. Even users with the admin role must also be granted security_admin to manage ACLs. In the base system, only the default system administrator has this role. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: The admin role alone cannot modify ACLs. Admins must also have security_admin for ACL management.
There is no standard role called 'acl_admin' in ServiceNow.
The itil role grants access to ITSM modules, not security administration.

source.excerpt: In the base system, only the default system administrator has the security admin role. Others with the admin role must also be granted the security admin role to manage ACLs.

questions.question: What happens when elevated privileges are activated in ServiceNow?

options.text: They remain active until manually deactivated
They last only for the current session and end with logout, timeout, or impersonation
They are permanently assigned to the user
They are shared with all members of the user's group

explanation.correct: Elevated roles last only for your session. They end with logout, session time out, or user impersonation. An upward arrow next to your avatar indicates activated elevated privileges. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Elevated privileges automatically end when the session ends, they don't require manual deactivation.
Elevated privileges are temporary by design for security purposes.
Elevated privileges apply only to the individual user who activated them.

source.excerpt: Elevated roles allow modification of the access control list. These roles last only for your session. They end with logout, session time out, or user impersonation.

questions.question: In what order does ServiceNow evaluate Access Control rules?

options.text: Allow rules first, then deny rules
Field access first, then table access
Deny rules first, then allow rules
Alphabetically by rule name

explanation.correct: The system checks deny rules first. If any deny rules conditions are unmet, access is blocked. Allow rules are evaluated only when no deny rules apply or if you meet all deny rule criteria. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Deny rules take precedence and are checked before allow rules.
Table access is checked first, then field access. The order is table-level before field-level.
ACL evaluation follows a specific security logic, not alphabetical order.

source.excerpt: The system checks deny rules first. If any deny rules conditions are unmet, access is blocked, requiring all matching deny rule conditions to be satisfied for access to proceed.

questions.question: What automatically happens when a new table is created in ServiceNow?

options.text: No security is applied by default
Access controls are automatically created for the table
Only admin users can access the table
The table is marked as read-only

explanation.correct: With system created access controls, it is rare to have a table with no access control rules. When a table is created, access controls are automatically created. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: ServiceNow automatically creates baseline access controls for new tables.
Access depends on the automatically created ACLs, not just admin restrictions.
New tables are not automatically read-only; access is controlled by ACLs.

source.excerpt: With system created access controls, it is rare to have a table with no access control rules. When a table is created, access controls are automatically created.

questions.question: A user passes a table-level ACL but fails a field-level ACL. What access does the user have?

options.text: Full access to the record including all fields
No access to the record at all
Access to the record but not to that specific field
Read-only access to all fields

explanation.correct: Access controls are checked in order, starting with table access and then field access. Failing a table rule denies access to all. Passing a table rule but failing a field rule denies access to that field only. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: The user would be denied access to the specific field that failed the ACL check.
Table-level access was granted, so the user can see the record, just not the restricted field.
The field restriction is specific to the failed ACL, not a global read-only state.

source.excerpt: Access controls are checked in order, starting with table access and then field access. Failing a table rule denies access to all passing a table rule, but failing a field rule denies access to that field.

questions.question: What does an upward arrow next to a user's avatar indicate in ServiceNow?

options.text: The user has unread notifications
The user has activated elevated privileges
The user is impersonating another user
The user has pending approvals

explanation.correct: An upward arrow next to your avatar indicates activated elevated privileges. This visual indicator helps administrators know when they have temporary elevated security access. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Unread notifications are indicated differently, typically with a badge number.
Impersonation is indicated by a different visual cue showing the impersonated user.
Pending approvals appear in the approval modules, not as avatar indicators.

source.excerpt: An upward arrow next to your avatar indicates activated elevated privileges.

questions.question: How do ACL rules for parent tables apply to child tables?

options.text: They don't apply - each table needs its own ACLs
ACL rules for parent tables apply to their child tables
Child tables override all parent table ACLs
Only admin-created ACLs are inherited

explanation.correct: ACL rules for parent tables apply to their child tables. This inheritance model means security settings on a parent table like 'task' automatically apply to child tables like 'incident' and 'change_request'. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: ACLs are inherited from parent to child tables in ServiceNow's table hierarchy.
Child tables don't automatically override parent ACLs; they inherit and can have additional ACLs.
All ACLs on parent tables are inherited, regardless of who created them.

source.excerpt: ACL rules for parent tables apply to their child tables.

questions.question: What are the three main security modules typically used by system administrators?

options.text: Users, Groups, and Roles
Security, ACL list, and High Security Settings
Authentication, Authorization, and Audit
Login, Password, and Session

explanation.correct: System administrators typically use three security modules: Security, ACL list, and High Security Settings. These modules provide the tools needed to manage access controls and security configurations. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: While Users, Groups, and Roles are important, they are not the three main security modules.
These are security concepts, not the specific module names in ServiceNow.
These relate to authentication features, not the main security administration modules.

source.excerpt: System administrators typically use three security modules-- security, ACL list, and high security settings.

questions.question: What limitation applies to users with the admin role when impersonating another user?

options.text: They cannot impersonate any users
They can only impersonate users in their group
They cannot impersonate the security_admin role or elevate privileges during impersonation
They must have manager approval to impersonate

explanation.correct: Admins cannot impersonate the security admin role or elevate privileges during impersonation to access high security functions. This is a security measure to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive security configurations. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Admins can impersonate other users, but with certain restrictions.
Impersonation is not limited to group membership for admins.
Manager approval is not required for admin impersonation by default.

source.excerpt: However, admins cannot impersonate the security admin role or elevate privileges during impersonation to access high security functions.

questions.question: Which components does ServiceNow use to ensure security for CRUD operations? (Choose two)

options.text: User authentication/login managed via users, groups, and roles
Automatic data encryption at rest
Application and module access controlled by roles
Mandatory two-factor authentication

explanation.correct: ServiceNow ensures security for CRUD operations with: user authentication/login managed via users, groups and roles; application and module access controlled by roles; and database access managed by system properties and table/field access controls. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: While encryption may be available, it's not one of the core CRUD security mechanisms described.
MFA is an optional security feature, not a core CRUD operation security mechanism.

source.excerpt: ServiceNow ensures security for CRUD operations with, user authentication/login, managed via users, groups and roles, application and module access controlled by roles.

questions.question: What is the purpose of user impersonation in ServiceNow?

options.text: To permanently change a user's password
To test the platform from another user's perspective and troubleshoot access issues
To delete another user's account
To merge two user accounts together

explanation.correct: Impersonation allows administrators to test the platform from another user's perspective. This is useful for troubleshooting access issues, verifying that security configurations work correctly, and understanding what a specific user can see and do.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Password changes are managed through user administration, not impersonation.
Account deletion is a separate administrative function, not related to impersonation.
Account merging is not a feature of impersonation.

source.excerpt: Impersonation allows administrators to test and troubleshoot by viewing the platform as another user would see it.

questions.question: What must a user have to access data in ServiceNow?

options.text: Only a role
Only ACL access
Both a role AND ACL access
Group membership only

explanation.correct: A user needs BOTH a role AND ACL access to see data. Roles grant access to application modules, while ACLs control record-level access. Both must be satisfied for a user to access specific data.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Roles alone grant module access but don't control data access without ACLs.
ACLs control data access but users also need appropriate roles to access modules.
Group membership helps organize users but doesn't directly grant data access without roles and ACLs.

source.excerpt: A user needs BOTH a role AND ACL access to see data. Roles grant access to application modules, while ACLs control record-level access.

questions.question: A system administrator needs to grant a user temporary elevated access to modify ACLs. What is the recommended approach?

options.text: Permanently assign the security_admin role to the user
Have the user activate elevated privileges for their session
Give the user the admin role
Disable all ACLs temporarily

explanation.correct: Elevated privileges allow temporary access to higher security functions and last only for the current session. This is more secure than permanently assigning roles because access automatically ends with logout, timeout, or impersonation. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Permanently assigning security_admin violates the principle of least privilege for temporary needs.
Admin role alone doesn't grant ACL modification - security_admin is still required.
Disabling ACLs would create significant security risks and is not recommended.

source.excerpt: Elevated roles allow modification of the access control list. These roles last only for your session.

questions.question: Which statements about the admin role in ServiceNow are true? (Choose two)

options.text: Admins have access to all platform features and can override access controls
Admins can automatically modify ACLs without any additional roles
The admin role should be assigned cautiously
Admins can impersonate security_admin during impersonation sessions

explanation.correct: Admins have access to all platform features and can override access controls, so the role should be assigned cautiously. However, admins cannot modify ACLs without security_admin and cannot impersonate security_admin during impersonation. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=8a89ef9447735ad4ca332a81736d432f&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Admins need the security_admin role in addition to admin to modify ACLs.
Admins cannot impersonate security_admin or elevate privileges during impersonation.

source.excerpt: Admins have access to all platform features and can override access controls so assign this role cautiously.

questions.question: What is the recommended method for assigning roles to users in ServiceNow?

options.text: Assign roles directly to individual user records
Add users to groups and assign roles to the groups
Use update sets to assign roles
Configure roles through the CMDB

explanation.correct: Rather than adding roles to individual users, the recommended approach is to add the user to a group and assign the role to the group. This makes maintenance easier when people transfer to different roles in the organization.

wrongAnswers.explanation: While possible, assigning roles directly to users makes maintenance difficult when organizational changes occur.
Update sets are for migrating configuration changes between instances, not for role assignment.
The CMDB tracks configuration items, not user roles.

questions.question: What indicates that elevated privileges are activated for an administrator's session?

options.text: A lock icon appears in the navigation menu
An upward arrow appears next to the user's avatar
The background color of the instance changes
A notification email is sent to the security team

explanation.correct: An upward arrow next to your avatar indicates activated elevated privileges. These roles last only for your session and end with logout, session timeout, or user impersonation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no lock icon for elevated privileges; the indicator is an upward arrow by the avatar.
The background color does not change for elevated privileges.
No email notification is sent when elevating privileges.

questions.question: In which order does ServiceNow evaluate access control rules?

options.text: Allow rules first, then deny rules
Field rules first, then table rules
Deny rules first, then allow rules if deny conditions are met
All rules are evaluated simultaneously

explanation.correct: The system checks deny rules first. If any deny rule conditions are unmet, access is blocked. Allow rules are evaluated only when no deny rules apply or if all deny rule criteria are satisfied.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Deny rules are checked before allow rules, not the other way around.
Access controls check table access first, then field access — but deny/allow ordering is the key evaluation sequence.
Rules are evaluated in a specific order: deny rules first, then allow rules.

questions.question: Which actions can users WITHOUT any assigned roles perform in ServiceNow? (Choose 2)

options.text: View a dashboard
Create business rules
Access the service catalog
Manage access control lists

explanation.correct: Users without any assigned roles can still log in and access common actions such as viewing a dashboard, accessing the service catalog, viewing knowledge articles, and taking surveys. These are often referred to as self-service users.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Creating business rules requires administrative roles.
Managing ACLs requires the security_admin role.

questions.question: Which statement about user impersonation is TRUE?

options.text: Any user can impersonate another user
Impersonation allows access to security incidents even if you don't have those roles
Only users with the admin or impersonator role can impersonate other users
Impersonation persists across multiple login sessions

explanation.correct: Only admins and users with the impersonator role can impersonate other users to test their access. When impersonating a user with a specific admin role, you cannot access certain features like security incidents unless you already have those roles.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Only users with the admin or impersonator role can impersonate others.
When impersonating, you cannot access features like security incidents unless you already have those specific roles.
Impersonation does not persist across login sessions.

questions.question: A user has the catalog_admin role. What access does this provide?

options.text: Only access to the Service Catalog application
Only access to user criteria modules
Access to all Service Catalog and user criteria modules, plus additional catalog_admin permissions
Full admin access to all platform features

explanation.correct: The catalog_admin role includes permissions from both user_criteria_admin and catalog roles, providing access to all applications and modules of both roles plus any permissions specific to catalog_admin.

wrongAnswers.explanation: catalog_admin includes more than just the catalog role — it also contains user_criteria_admin permissions.
catalog_admin includes user criteria access but also catalog and additional permissions.
catalog_admin provides access to catalog-related features, not full admin access.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the ServiceNow Security Center?

options.text: To manage user passwords and authentication only
To monitor security compliance, manage hardening settings, and run security scans
To configure firewalls and network security
To create and manage encryption keys

explanation.correct: ServiceNow Security Center is a built-in tool that helps system administrators manage and improve instance security. It includes hardening checks, security scanning, customer actions, notifications, and compliance scoring.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Security Center covers much more than passwords — it includes hardening, scanning, compliance, and metrics.
Security Center focuses on instance security settings, not network infrastructure.
Encryption key management is not the primary purpose of Security Center.
